ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, there are two line segments AD and BC intersecting at point E, forming the left triangle ABE and the right triangle DCE. The left side AB is labeled 2, the right side CD is labeled 5, and AB and CD have the same arrow markings on them, indicating AB ∥ CD. Line segment AE is labeled x−1, and line segment ED is labeled x+5. Then reason: Because AD and BC intersect at E, ∠AEB and ∠DEC are vertical angles and are equal. Also because AB ∥ CD, a pair of corresponding angles can be obtained as equal, therefore △ABE ∼ △DCE. Corresponding sides are proportional: AE/ED = AB/CD, so (x−1)/(x+5) = 2/5. Solve the equation: 5(x−1)=2(x+5), 5x−5=2x+10, 3x=15, x=5. Therefore AE=x−1=5−1=4.
